blocks.text: Comparing the entropies of reactants and products explains the size and sign of the entropy change of a reaction. When a solid becomes a liquid or a gas in the products, the entropy change is positive; if there are more moles in the products, the entropy change is positive; and a change in the number of gaseous molecules matters most, because gases have high entropies, the more gas molecules the more ways of arranging them. For CaCO3(s) giving CaO(s) + CO2(g) the entropy of the system increases because a gas (high entropy) is produced from a solid (low entropy); such reactions are spontaneous. For 2N2O5(g) giving 4NO2(g) + O2(g) the entropy increases because there are five moles of gas in the products against two in the reactants, also a spontaneous process. Dissolving sugar in tea increases the entropy of both solute and solvent.
The sign of the entropy change and spontaneity

The entropy of a substance is always positive, but an entropy change may be positive or negative. A positive delta S means a spontaneous process; a negative delta S implies more ordered molecules and a decrease in disorder. For some reactions, however, the entropy change fails to tell about spontaneity, and another quantity, free energy, is needed.
